summary: For b false both sides are the reduction; for b true use kᴴJk = J over Ô, transpose and reduce modulo w.

steps.claim: Case b = false: both sides are the reduction s_w of k (definitional). Case b = true: write k as coming from an integral matrix g with the membership e.
steps.lean: ⟨k, k.2⟩ = S.idOrInvAdjoint b (S.reduction k i w) := b.rec rfl (k.rec fun k ⟨g, e⟩ ↦ by

steps.claim: The element k comes from an element g of the unitary group of latMiddle(S, Ô).splitGram over the integral finite adeles Ô (U.mem_range_map: Ô → 𝔸_f is injective and maps the integral Gram matrix to the adelic one).
steps.lean:
obtain ⟨g, -, ⟨⟩⟩ :=
    U.mem_range_map (by simp) (Ô E).subtype_injective isUnit (S.map_splitGram_latMiddle _) congr($e)

steps.claim: For g ∈ U(J) over Ô, J g⁻¹ = gᴴ J (U.form_mul_inv_eq); transposing (J is symmetric) and reducing modulo w gives that the conjugate ḡ reduces to J⁻¹((g mod w)ᵀ)⁻¹J, which is idOrInvAdjoint(true) of the reduction of k at w.
